data.content_ref: inline:SRC_03's 'known generative model' requirement narrows the task class to atypical cases where the posterior is accessible, but the problem asks about tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes broadly—most such tasks (medical diagnosis, fault prediction) have verifiable outcomes yet unknown generative models. Under that scope, 'the checklist is necessarily a lossy compression of the generative model' is unsupported: without a known generative model the checklist's bias relative to it is undefined, so the claimed distinguishing evidence—systematic error on codec-divergent items—cannot be isolated in a single evaluation.
